questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague on a technical approach. How did you resolve it?
questions.zh: 讲一次你和同事在技术方案上意见不合的经历。你们是怎么解决的？
outline: Situation: the decision at stake and both positions, described fairly
Task: why the outcome mattered to you and the project
Action: listened first, then compared options with data or a prototype
Result: what was decided and how the working relationship held up
Reflection: how you approach disagreements now

chunks.zh: 看法一致（常用于否定句）
保留不同意见，但全力执行决定

followUps: What if you had still disagreed after the decision was made?

questions.prompt: Describe a time you pushed back on a product requirement. What happened?
questions.zh: 讲一次你对产品需求提出反对的经历。后来怎么样了？
outline: Situation: the requirement and why it worried you
Task: protect the timeline or quality without simply saying no
Action: explained the cost in plain terms, offered a cheaper alternative
Result: what shipped and how the product manager reacted
followUps: How do you decide when a requirement is worth fighting over?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision your manager made.
questions.zh: 讲一次你不同意经理所做决定的经历。
outline: Situation: the decision and why you saw it differently
Task: raise your concern without undermining your manager
Action: made your case privately, with evidence, then listened
Result: whether the decision changed, and how you supported it

chunks.zh: 我还没被说服……（委婉表示怀疑）
摆出理由论证（某事值得做）
保留不同意见，但全力执行决定

questions.prompt: Tell me about a project that failed or didn't go the way you planned.
questions.zh: 讲一个失败了、或者没有按你的计划走的项目。
outline: Situation: the project goal and what was at stake
Task: your part in it; own your share honestly
Action: what you tried once you saw it going wrong
Result: the actual outcome, without sugar-coating
Reflection: the lesson and how you applied it later

chunks.term: If I were to do it again, I would ...

followUps: What were the early warning signs that you missed?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a mistake you made that caused a problem in production. How did you handle it?
questions.zh: 讲一次你犯的错导致线上出问题的经历。你是怎么处理的？
outline: Situation: what you changed and what broke
Task: limit the damage first, explain later
Action: rolled back, told the team right away, traced the cause
Result: impact on users and how long recovery took
Reflection: the safeguard you added so it cannot recur
followUps: How did your team react when you told them?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to deliver something under a very tight deadline.
questions.zh: 讲一次你必须在非常紧的期限内交付的经历。
outline: Situation: the deadline, why it was fixed, what was at risk
Task: what you had to deliver and with whom
Action: cut scope, reordered the work, kept stakeholders informed
Result: what shipped on time and what was deferred
Reflection: what you would plan differently next time

chunks.term: separate the must-haves from the nice-to-haves
chunks.zh: 把必须做的和锦上添花的分开

followUps: Looking back, was the deadline actually necessary?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you realized you weren't going to hit a deadline. What did you do?
questions.zh: 讲一次你意识到自己赶不上截止日期的经历。你是怎么做的？
outline: Situation: the commitment and when you saw the slip coming
Task: reset expectations while there was still time to react
Action: raised it early, with options rather than just bad news
Result: the new plan and how stakeholders responded
Reflection: how your estimates changed afterwards

chunks.zh: 这件事比预期花的时间长。
尽早把（风险、问题）提出来

chunks.term: I should have it done by ...

questions.prompt: Walk me through a serious production incident you were involved in. What was your role?
questions.zh: 讲一次你参与处理的严重线上事故。你在其中是什么角色？
outline: Situation: what failed, who was affected, how you found out
Task: your role, such as incident lead or investigator
Action: mitigated first, communicated status, then found the cause
Result: time to recovery and customer impact
Reflection: postmortem findings and the follow-up work
followUps: How do you keep a postmortem from turning into blame?

questions.prompt: Tell me about the hardest bug you've ever had to track down.
questions.zh: 讲讲你排查过的最难的一个 bug。
outline: Situation: the symptom and why it was hard to reproduce
Task: why it fell to you and what was at stake
Action: how you narrowed it down step by step
Result: the root cause, the fix, and how you verified it
Reflection: the tooling or tests you added afterwards

chunks.term: The first thing I did was ...

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you inherited a codebase in poor shape. How did you approach it?
questions.zh: 讲一次你接手一个质量很差的代码库的经历。你是怎么着手的？
outline: Situation: what you took over and what made it risky
Task: keep delivering features while making it safer to change
Action: added tests around critical paths, refactored incrementally
Result: fewer incidents or faster delivery, with numbers if possible
Reflection: why you did not push for a full rewrite

chunks.zh: 用单元测试把它覆盖到
绞杀者模式（逐步替换旧系统）
摆出理由论证（某事值得做）

followUps: How did you decide what to refactor and what to leave alone?

questions.prompt: Describe a time you had to deliver something when the requirements were vague or incomplete.
questions.zh: 讲一次在需求模糊或者不完整的情况下，你仍然要交付的经历。
outline: Situation: what was asked and what was unclear
Task: turn a fuzzy goal into something you could build
Action: asked targeted questions, wrote down assumptions, shipped a thin slice
Result: how early feedback shaped the final version

chunks.term: Just to make sure I understand, ...
chunks.zh: 我确认一下我理解得对不对，……

chunks.term: Is it safe to assume that ...?

chunks.zh: 核心使用场景、核心用例

chunks.term: I'll leave ... out of scope for now.
chunks.zh: 我先把……放在讨论范围之外。

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you convinced your team to adopt a new technology or way of working.
questions.zh: 讲一次你说服团队采用一项新技术或新做法的经历。
outline: Situation: the pain point the team had learned to live with
Task: get skeptical teammates to try something new
Action: built a small proof of concept, shared results, addressed concerns
Result: adoption and the measurable improvement
Reflection: what actually changed people's minds

chunks.zh: 摆出理由论证（某事值得做）
概念验证（证明方案可行的小样）
赞成、愿意一起推进（某个方案）

followUps: Was there anyone you never managed to convince?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex technical problem to a non-technical stakeholder.
questions.zh: 讲一次你需要向不懂技术的相关方解释复杂技术问题的经历。
outline: Situation: the technical issue and who needed to understand it
Task: get a decision from them, not teach them engineering
Action: dropped the jargon, used an analogy, framed it as business impact
Result: the decision they made and whether it held up

chunks.zh: 从总体上讲、不涉及细节地说
换算成、转化为（业务结果）

chunks.term: Let me give you a concrete example.
chunks.zh: 我给你举个具体的例子。

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you received critical feedback. How did you respond?
questions.zh: 讲一次你收到批评性反馈的经历。你是怎么回应的？
outline: Situation: who gave the feedback and what it was about
Task: understand it properly instead of defending yourself
Action: asked for specifics, reflected, changed one concrete habit
Result: what improved and how you checked back

chunks.term: Could you give me an example?
An area I'm working on is ...
chunks.zh: 我正在改进的一个方面是……

followUps: Was there any part of the feedback you disagreed with?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to give difficult feedback to a peer.
questions.zh: 讲一次你不得不给同级同事提难以开口的反馈的经历。
outline: Situation: the behavior or work that was causing problems
Task: raise it honestly without damaging the relationship
Action: spoke privately, used specific examples, asked for their view
Result: what changed afterwards
Reflection: what you learned about giving feedback

chunks.term: Let me give you a concrete example.
chunks.zh: 我给你举个具体的例子。

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had several urgent tasks competing for your attention. How did you decide what to do first?
questions.zh: 讲一次好几件紧急的事同时压过来的经历。你是怎么决定先做哪件的？
outline: Situation: the competing demands and who was waiting on each
Task: decide the order and manage expectations
Action: ranked by impact and urgency, delegated, renegotiated one deadline
Result: what got done and what you knowingly let slip

chunks.zh: 把任务放手交给别人做

questions.prompt: Describe a situation where two stakeholders wanted conflicting things from you. How did you handle it?
questions.zh: 讲一次两个相关方对你提出互相冲突的要求的情况。你是怎么处理的？
outline: Situation: who wanted what, and why both could not win
Task: reach a decision without picking sides behind anyone's back
Action: clarified the real goals, got both in one room, proposed options
Result: the compromise or the escalation, and the outcome

chunks.zh: 把（某人）拉进来，让其知情或参与
升级（把问题上报给更合适的人）

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to pick up an unfamiliar technology quickly to deliver a project.
questions.zh: 讲一次你为了交付项目必须快速学会一门陌生技术的经历。
outline: Situation: the project and the technology you did not know
Task: become productive fast enough to hit the date
Action: learned by building, read the source, asked experts early
Result: what you delivered and how solid it was
Reflection: how you learn new things in general

chunks.term: I haven't used ... in production, but ...
chunks.zh: 我没在生产环境用过……，不过……

chunks.term: The first thing I did was ...

chunks.zh: 深入钻研、深入展开（某个部分）

chunks.term: good enough for our use case
chunks.zh: 对我们的场景来说已经够用

followUps: How do you decide how deep to go when time is short?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you noticed a problem nobody owned and decided to fix it yourself.
questions.zh: 讲一次你发现一个没人管的问题、并决定自己动手解决的经历。
outline: Situation: the problem everyone complained about but nobody fixed
Task: nobody asked you; explain why you stepped up
Action: sized the problem, got agreement, did the work alongside your roadmap
Result: time saved or failures avoided, ideally with numbers

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to compromise on quality in order to ship on time.
questions.zh: 讲一次你为了按时上线而不得不在质量上让步的经历。
outline: Situation: the deadline and the shortcut on the table
Task: ship without creating a risk you could not contain
Action: chose which corners to cut, documented the debt, added safeguards
Result: shipped on time; what happened to the debt afterwards
Reflection: where you draw the line on shortcuts

chunks.zh: 考虑到当时的限制条件
建一个任务单（记下来以后处理）
回头再来处理、过后再谈

followUps: Did you ever go back and fix it?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to work closely with someone you found difficult to work with.
questions.zh: 讲一次你必须和一个你觉得很难相处的人紧密合作的经历。
outline: Situation: the working relationship and how it affected delivery
Task: make the collaboration work; you still had to ship together
Action: tried to understand their side, agreed on how to work together
Result: how the work and the relationship turned out
Reflection: what you learned about your own style

chunks.zh: 看法一致（常用于否定句）
所以你的意思是……（复述对方的话）
（临时）开个语音或视频聊一下

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to make an important decision without having all the information you wanted.
questions.zh: 讲一次你在信息不全的情况下必须做出重要决定的经历。
outline: Situation: the decision, the time pressure, what was unknown
Task: you were the one who had to decide
Action: listed assumptions, estimated the risk, picked the reversible option
Result: how it played out and what you adjusted

chunks.zh: 考虑到当时的限制条件
大致的数字、粗略的估计值

followUps: What would have made you delay the decision instead?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you were convinced you were right and turned out to be wrong.
questions.zh: 讲一次你坚信自己是对的、结果发现自己错了的经历。
outline: Situation: the position you held and why you were confident
Task: stay open even though you had argued strongly
Action: looked at the new evidence, admitted it, switched approach
Result: the better outcome that followed
Reflection: how you test your own assumptions now

chunks.zh: 故意唱反调（为了检验方案）

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a request from a colleague or another team.
questions.zh: 讲一次你不得不拒绝同事或其他团队的请求的经历。
outline: Situation: the request and why you could not take it on
Task: decline while keeping the relationship intact
Action: explained your priorities, offered an alternative or a later date
Result: how they took it and what happened to the request

chunks.term: I'll get back to you on that.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time your work was blocked by another team. How did you move things forward?
questions.zh: 讲一次你的工作被别的团队卡住的经历。你是怎么推动事情往前走的？
outline: Situation: the dependency and why the other team was not delivering
Task: hit your date without owning their backlog
Action: understood their constraints, offered help, found a workaround, escalated last
Result: how you got unblocked and the effect on the timeline

chunks.zh: 我在等……（别人的结果或答复）
让（某人）能继续干活、解除阻塞
升级（把问题上报给更合适的人）

questions.prompt: Why are you looking for a change right now?
questions.zh: 你为什么现在想换工作？
outline: Current role is outsourced project work; scope and stack are fixed
Eight years in, I want end-to-end ownership of a product
Remote team means a longer-term home, not another rotation
Frame it as moving toward growth, never complaints about now

chunks.zh: 逐步成长到能胜任（某个角色），g 开头的短语动词
略超出现有能力、能逼人成长的任务

chunks.term: I'd like to take on more ...
chunks.zh: 我想承担更多……（职责、挑战）
我有兴趣转向……（某个方向或角色）

followUps: What would make you stay in a role for three years or more?
What are you hoping this role gives you that your current one doesn't?

questions.prompt: Why do you want to work remotely?
questions.zh: 你为什么想做远程工作？
outline: Written async communication is my strength: strong reader and writer
I document decisions and put agreements in writing by default
Deep-work hours let me own problems end to end
I am looking for a team to stay with for years

chunks.zh: 主动把……的责任担起来（含 o 开头的名词）
落实到书面、白纸黑字写下来

followUps: How do you handle time-zone differences with a team?
How do you stay visible and connected when nobody sees you in an office?

questions.prompt: What motivates you to do your best work?
questions.zh: 什么能激励你把工作做到最好？
outline: Real users depending on what I ship
Hard problems with the autonomy to solve them properly
Fast, honest feedback loops so I can adjust quickly
Example: owned an internal platform where AI features cut manual test-case work

chunks.zh: 主动把……的责任担起来（含 o 开头的名词）
略超出现有能力、能逼人成长的任务
谢谢你的反馈。（a 开头的动词，比 thanks 郑重）

followUps: What kind of work drains you instead?
Tell me about a project where you felt this motivation strongly.

questions.prompt: Where do you see yourself in three to five years?
questions.zh: 你觉得三到五年后你会在什么位置？
outline: Senior or staff-level individual contributor, not the management track
Owning a product area end to end, from design to operations
Deeper systems skills on top of my frontend depth
Fully fluent working in an English-speaking team day to day

chunks.zh: 不带人的技术岗（和管理岗相对，两个词，常缩写成 IC）
逐步成长到能胜任（某个角色），g 开头的短语动词
主动把……的责任担起来（含 o 开头的名词）
我有兴趣转向……（某个方向或角色）

followUps: What skills are you actively building to get there?
How does this role fit into that plan?

questions.prompt: What's your greatest weakness?
questions.zh: 你最大的弱点是什么？
outline: Spoken English fluency under pressure; reading and writing are strong
I train speaking daily with a structured output system, and it shows
Second one: I used to take on too much before asking for help
Now I raise risks early in standups instead of silently absorbing them

chunks.zh: 盲区（自己意识不到的弱点）
这点我会改进。（w 开头的短语动词）

chunks.term: What could I have done better?
chunks.zh: 我当时哪里可以做得更好？
提前知会、打个招呼提醒一声

followUps: How is that weakness going to affect your work here?
What is your plan to improve it over the next six months?

questions.prompt: Why should we hire you over other candidates?
questions.zh: 我们为什么应该选你，而不是其他候选人？
outline: Eight years shipping real commercial systems across the stack
I write clearly, which makes me easy to work with asynchronously
I take ownership end to end; example: the LLM test-case platform
Honest about depth: Rust and Python are personal projects, and I say so

chunks.zh: 主动把……的责任担起来（含 o 开头的名词）
落实到书面、白纸黑字写下来

followUps: What would your first ninety days look like here?
Is there anything in your background that concerns us that you'd like to address?

questions.prompt: Tell me about the worst production incident you personally caused. What happened, and what changed afterwards?
questions.zh: 讲讲你亲手造成过的最严重的一次生产事故。发生了什么、之后改了什么？
outline: Set the scene: what you shipped and when
Say plainly which decision was yours
Walk the timeline to detection and mitigation
Name the preventive measure that followed
End with the lesson you still apply

chunks.zh: 宣告事故（正式拉响事故流程）
根本原因分析（复盘的核心动作）
经验教训（复盘的沉淀小节）
无指责复盘稿（写系统不写人）

followUps: What did you tell the affected users?
How long did it take you to tell your manager?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you were confidently wrong in front of your team. How did it play out?
questions.zh: 讲讲你曾经在团队面前自信满满却错了的一次。后来怎么样？
outline: State your wrong position, unvarnished
Say who challenged it and with what evidence
Admit the moment you knew: that one's on me
Describe swallowing your pride in the review
Share the check you added to your thinking

chunks.zh: 那件事怪我、是我的责任

followUps: Did anyone lose trust in you over it?
How do you test your confidence now?

questions.prompt: Tell me about critical feedback you initially disagreed with. Where did it end up?
questions.zh: 讲讲你一开始不认同的一次严厉反馈。最后怎么样了？
outline: Quote the feedback fairly, not defensively
Admit your first reaction honestly
Describe clearing the air with the giver
Name the behavior that actually changed
Say what the feedback missed, with respect

chunks.zh: 给出建设性反馈（对事不对人）
把（批评）往心里去、当成针对个人
把话说开、消除误会或紧张气氛

followUps: How long did the change take?
Do you still disagree with part of it?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a project you built that was cancelled or never shipped. What did you take from it?
questions.zh: 讲讲你做过的一个被砍掉或从未上线的项目。你从中得到了什么？
outline: Explain what it was and why it started
Say what went poorly in the signals you missed
Admit where you got lucky it died early
Name the follow-up action in your next project
Frame the lesson without bitterness

chunks.zh: 做得差的地方（复盘的固定小节）
我们走运的地方（差点更糟的环节）
经验教训（复盘的沉淀小节）
跟进行动（复盘后要做的改进项）

followUps: When did you first suspect it would die?
What would have saved it?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a serious disagreement with your manager. How did it end?
questions.zh: 讲讲你和上级发生过的一次严重分歧。最后怎么收场的？
outline: State both positions in their strongest form
Say how you brought it up, not around it
Describe the hard conversation itself
Agree to disagree where the data ran out
Name what the relationship looks like now

chunks.zh: 求同存异、各自保留意见

followUps: What would you do differently in the first conversation?
Did you ever consider going over their head?
